PullRequest.Title: Suggest agent session storage cleanup when worktrees accumulate
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/338039

## Why

Before auto-archive-on-PR-merge settings existed, sessions accumulated and their worktrees now consume significant disk space. Users have no visibility into this and no guided way to clean it up.

## What

**Suggestion notice** — appears below the Sessions list when cleanup is worthwhile:
- 20+ *eligible* worktrees exist, **or**
- eligible inactive worktrees can reclaim 5 GiB or more

Only eligible candidates count toward the worktree threshold, so the notice is always actionable.

**Manage Agent Session Storage editor** — review and clean up eligible sessions, with an inactivity-days filter (7/15/30/60/90), a worktree-only filter, and a toggle for the suggestion itself. Only fully eligible sessions are listed.

## Dismissal and reset

| Action | Effect |
|---|---|
| `X` or `Escape` | Suppressed for the current window only |
| **Don't Show Again** | Sets the setting to `false` at application scope |
| Opening the manager | Suppressed for the current window |

Measurements are cached for one hour; changing the days filter recomputes from cache without re-measuring disk.

## Settings

`chat.agentSessions.sessionStorageCleanupSuggestion.enabled` gates the notice.

## Accessibility

- The notice is a labeled region, fully keyboard navigable, and announced once to screen readers.
- **Disable Session Storage Cleanup Suggestions** command gives screen reader users a non-visual equivalent of **Don't Show Again**.
- The manager is reachable from the Command Palette and the session context menu.
- The flow is documented in the Sessions accessibility help dialog.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` — clean
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — clean
- 45 focused tests passing across the service, configuration, notice, banners, and accessibility help

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed call path from manager/notice to getSessionWorktreeDiskUsage to these protocol calls is explicit, and repository protocol implementations prove one request and filesystem stat per entry. Exact tree sizes vary, but large dependency trees are realistic and the concurrency is mathematically unbounded by entry count.
Findings.PerformanceResource: agent-host protocol requests and filesystem stat operations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each worktree now performs one resourceList request per directory and one resourceResolve request per child entry. The Promise.all concurrency grows with every child in each of up to 8 directories, multiplied again by all worktrees in up to 2 concurrently measured sessions.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: protocol/host I/O saturation, high CPU/allocation pressure, and long manager load times or interference with active agent traffic
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, opening the cleanup manager or Sessions view did not recursively stat worktree contents, so this protocol and filesystem load did not exist.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new recursive measurement maps every directory entry to resourceResolve inside Promise.all; MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS limits directory batches but does not limit the number of child stat requests, and the provider concurrently starts every worktree traversal for a session.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added lines 38-40 create Promise.all(children.entries.map(...resourceResolve...)); this is the new unbounded per-entry request burst.
Findings.Title: Bound per-entry worktree stat requests
Findings.Impact: Opening Clean Up Agent Worktrees on a cold cache—or enabling the Sessions cleanup suggestion—can launch thousands or tens of thousands of simultaneous protocol requests for a large source tree (for example a worktree containing node_modules). The manager awaits the traversal, while the background suggestion scan can contend with normal agent traffic.
Findings.Evidence: resourceList is implemented as a protocol _sendRequest and returns all immediate entries; resourceResolve is another _sendRequest backed by IFileService.stat. At lines 38-41, every child from each batched directory is resolved through one Promise.all. BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider also uses Promise.all across a session's worktrees, while SessionWorktreeCleanupService permits two sessions concurrently, so the aggregate is not bounded by the apparent directory batch of 8.
Findings.Recommendation: Use one shared limiter for resourceResolve work across directories/worktrees (and ideally sessions), or add/use a host-side aggregate disk-usage operation so only one bounded request crosses the protocol per worktree.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The ordering and downstream eligibility filter are explicit in changed code, and the provider implementation proves each call recursively traverses the worktree. Magnitude depends on retained session/tree counts, but this feature targets users with accumulated worktrees, making multi-root scans the intended scenario.
Findings.PerformanceResource: recursive filesystem walks, agent-host IPC requests, and filesystem stat operations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cold-scan cost is the sum of every file and directory in every session that has a worktree, including active, running, needs-input, pinned, recent, archived, untitled, and errored sessions; it therefore grows with all retained worktrees rather than only cleanup candidates.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: excessive I/O/IPC and delayed cleanup-manager loading, with hourly background contention when suggestions are enabled
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no disk-usage scan when opening the cleanup UI or Sessions view.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: _measureWorktrees filters only for the presence of a worktree, invokes the recursive getDiskUsage for every such session, and computes cleanupState only after the traversal. The editor subsequently renders only cleanupState === 'eligible' rows, so protected sessions' measurements are discarded.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 184 invokes the new recursive disk measurement for every item selected only by worktree presence at lines 168-171, before the eligibility classification at line 193.
Findings.Title: Classify protected sessions before measuring them
Findings.Impact: A user opening the manager with many recent or protected agent sessions must wait for complete recursive scans that cannot produce a selectable row. With suggestions enabled, opening the Sessions view repeats this cold work at the hourly cache boundary even when few or no sessions are eligible.
Findings.Evidence: Lines 168-171 collect all worktree sessions without eligibility checks; line 184 awaits getSessionWorktreeDiskUsage; only line 193 calls _getCleanupState. That state rejects archived/active/running/needs-input/pinned/recent/untitled/error sessions. SessionWorktreeCleanupEditor.setInput awaits getWorktrees and renderRows explicitly iterates only eligible rows, proving the extra boundary work is on the manager critical path and unused by the UI.
Findings.Recommendation: Compute all metadata-only protection states first and call getSessionWorktreeDiskUsage only for sessions that can be cleanup candidates; preserve summary counts from workspace metadata without traversing protected trees.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The two concurrently reachable changed entry points and absence of a shared measurement promise are explicit. The trigger requires suggestions enabled and quick manager opening, so prevalence is uncertain, but whenever it occurs the full duplicate traversal is deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: duplicate recursive filesystem walks and duplicate agent-host protocol requests
Findings.PerformanceScaling: When two cold callers overlap, each independently traverses every worktree and performs one list per directory plus one stat per entry, doubling work proportional to the total files across all retained worktrees.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: avoidable I/O/IPC saturation and increased manager load latency during the initial suggestion scan
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR neither the automatic storage scan nor manager measurement existed, so there was no duplicate traversal race.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: _refreshIfNeeded coalesces only callers entering the automatic refresh path. The editor calls getWorktrees directly; while _refresh is still measuring, _lastMeasuredWorktrees is unset, so _getMeasuredWorktrees starts a second _measureWorktrees call instead of joining the in-flight one.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 223 directly awaits a new _measureWorktrees call whenever the completed-result cache is empty, even if the automatic refresh has the same measurement in flight.
Findings.Title: Coalesce concurrent worktree measurements
Findings.Impact: With suggestions enabled, SessionsView immediately starts a background scan. If the user opens Clean Up Agent Worktrees from the always-available command or menu before that scan completes—a likely interval for large trees—the editor launches the same expensive scan again and waits behind competing duplicate I/O.
Findings.Evidence: SessionStorageCleanupNotice line 97 fire-and-forgets activate(), while SessionWorktreeCleanupEditor line 161 independently awaits getWorktrees(). The only in-flight field is _refreshPromise in _refreshIfNeeded; line 223 in _getMeasuredWorktrees directly starts _measureWorktrees and stores results only after it finishes, leaving the second entry point uncoalesced.
Findings.Recommendation: Track a shared in-flight measurement promise inside _getMeasuredWorktrees, keyed by the measured session signature as needed, and have both refresh and editor callers await it before starting another scan.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Sessions view with storage-cleanup suggestions enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SessionStorageCleanupNotice starts activate() without awaiting it, so the scan is off the initial DOM/render critical path, but it competes with active agent protocol and filesystem work; the notice cannot appear until measurement completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: resourceList protocol request backed by filesystem directory resolution
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per traversed directory across every measured worktree; all worktree-bearing sessions are measured, two sessions at a time.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The Sessions view did not inspect worktree contents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off initial rendering but required before the suggestion can appear and able to contend with normal agent-host traffic.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: resourceResolve protocol request backed by IFileService.stat
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One root stat plus one stat for every child entry; child requests are unbounded within each of up to 8 current directories and multiplied by concurrent worktrees/sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No per-entry worktree stat requests were made by the Sessions view.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off initial rendering, but large bursts can saturate the protocol/host filesystem and delay both the suggestion and unrelated agent work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All loaded sessions containing one or more distinct worktree URIs, and recursively every directory entry in those worktrees; effective cardinality is not reduced to the old, inactive cleanup candidates.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The service limits measurements to 2 sessions, but each session starts all of its worktrees with Promise.all. Each worktree processes up to 8 directories while each directory starts resourceResolve for every child concurrently, so aggregate stat concurrency is unbounded by directory width and worktrees per session.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A completed measurement is reused for one hour when the sorted session/worktree signature is unchanged; state such as age and activity is recomputed from cached sizes. Automatic refresh callers share _refreshPromise, but the completed cache is cold on first activation and after archive invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed activation path, recursive calls, protocol implementations, and multiplicative concurrency are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact retained-session counts and filesystem widths vary, and the setting defaults off for users without a migrated/experimental enablement; dependency trees with thousands of entries and users with accumulated worktrees are nevertheless the feature's target population.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the scan traverses protected sessions that cannot contribute and uses unbounded per-entry protocol concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Clean Up Agent Worktrees and change the inactivity-days filter
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SessionWorktreeCleanupEditor.setInput awaits load(), which awaits getWorktrees(), so a cold measurement blocks rows and summary from appearing. Filter changes call load again; after a completed warm measurement they only recompute state and rerender.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recursive resourceList/resourceResolve traversal for worktree sizes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For each worktree session, one list per directory and one stat per entry, including active/recent/running/pinned/archived/error sessions; duplicate full cardinality if editor opening overlaps automatic activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No cleanup editor or worktree-size traversal existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly blocks manager data from rendering on a cold cache.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cold cost covers files/directories in all worktree sessions, not just eligible sessions. Warm rendering scales with measured sessions and DOM rows scale with eligible sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cold traversal has the same 2-session outer limiter but unbounded worktree/per-entry inner concurrency. If the automatic suggestion scan is already running, the editor does not join it and starts a second full traversal. Warm filter changes are in-memory and effectively serialized by renderVersion, though superseded loads are not cancelled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Completed sizes are cached for one hour by session/worktree signature, so changing 7/15/30/60/90 days normally avoids I/O. There is no shared in-flight measurement cache between activate() and getWorktrees(), producing duplicate cold scans on overlap.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: setInput awaits the service, the eligibility decision occurs after traversal, and the missing shared in-flight promise is explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Warm-cache opens and filter changes are cheap; cold duration depends on repository count, tree size, host locality, and whether an automatic scan overlaps.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: protected-session fan-out and missing cold-scan coalescing delay the manager; warm filter recomputation itself is acceptable.

Scenarios.Scenario: Select eligible sessions and clean up their worktrees
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After confirmation, cleanupWorktrees serially awaits archiveSession for each selected session; the editor then awaits load(). Archive state dispatch is per selected session, while actual worktree cleanup is described as background. Archive events invalidate the size cache, so the subsequent load performs a cold measurement.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: SessionIsArchivedChanged dispatch to the owning agent host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dispatch per selected session, serialized by cleanupWorktrees.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Users could archive sessions individually, but this bulk cleanup path did not issue a sequence from the manager.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The management method awaits each archive call, though the base provider dispatch itself is immediate and background cleanup is not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A fresh full traversal after cache invalidation, again covering all worktree sessions and entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no manager post-cleanup scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the manager refresh after cleanup and is covered by the protected-session traversal finding.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Archive operations scale with selected sessions/worktrees. The post-action reload again scales with all retained worktree contents, including newly archived sessions while their background deletion may still be pending.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Archive calls are intentionally serialized by the for/await loop. The subsequent scan uses the same 2-session outer limiter and unbounded internal stat fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Every archive event resets _lastMeasurementAt, discarding the completed one-hour measurement; the immediate editor reload therefore cannot use cached sizes. No incremental removal of selected sessions is applied.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for serialization, cache invalidation, and immediate reload; exact background deletion timing is not established and was not used as a separate finding.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Selected counts and timing of host-side deletion vary; archive dispatch itself is lightweight for the inspected agent-host provider, while the post-action scan dominates large repositories.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding for serialized archive dispatch; the expensive post-cleanup traversal is already captured by the protected-session measurement finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and interact with the eligible-session table on a warm cache
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After cached data resolves, renderRows synchronously filters, sorts eligible rows, creates row DOM/listeners, reads scroll dimensions once, and updates the action state. Checkbox changes update only selection/button state; Select All rerenders rows.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: CPU and DOM objects scale with eligible sessions, while sort is O(E log E). The feature threshold starts at 20 and accumulated installations may have more, but no concrete repository evidence establishes a cardinality at which this alone causes jank.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI-thread work; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operations occur on the warm render path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses the service's completed one-hour measurement; age-filter changes recompute cleanup state from cached sizes and rerender without remeasurement.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for linear DOM creation, insufficient for a standalone performance regression at established realistic scale.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Eligible-row counts can be large, but expected real-world upper bounds and measured render cost are unavailable.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: synchronous work is bounded by visible eligible candidates and lacks concrete evidence of user-visible jank independent of the reported measurement costs.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 26 changed files and all diff pages. Submitted three introduced regressions: unbounded per-entry stat concurrency, recursive measurement of sessions that cannot be cleanup candidates, and duplicate cold scans when manager opening overlaps automatic activation. No concrete regression-fix learning signal was present.
